tools.name: fetch
tools.title: Fetch a record
tools.description: Read one full record (an answer, Action, prompt or page) by the citeladder:// id another read returned. Never construct an id.

id.description: A citeladder:// id exactly as a read returned it.

tools.name: get_project_business_context
tools.title: Get project overview
tools.description: Read one overview of a project in a single call: its identity and markets (with the market ids other tools take), then a short summary per section: business profile with owned domains and tracked competitors, latest visibility, the top 10 Actions, active prompts, Site Health, AI crawler access, demand, search performance, AI referrals, crawler logs, connected data and keyword research. Use it first to orient yourself, then the matching read_* tool for depth or paging (each section is that tool's default read). Omit sections for all of them; pass a few to keep the response small. A section can be unavailable on its own, such as a project with no completed run.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

sections.description: The sections to read; omit for all. profile also returns owned domains and competitors.

tools.name: list_projects
tools.title: List projects
tools.description: List the projects this connection can read. Start here when no project is known: every other project tool needs the id it returns. Each project has its id, name, brand, website, industry, primary market and the workspace it belongs to. Projects come oldest first, 50 per page by default; pass next_cursor for more. An empty list means no workspace was approved for this connection. To find a project by name use search; for one project in depth use get_project_business_context.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: open_analytics
tools.title: Open CiteLadder
tools.description: Show the user the CiteLadder project picker, in clients that display apps, so they can choose a project to view. Use list_projects to find projects yourself.

tools.name: read_actions
tools.title: Read Actions
tools.description: List the work CiteLadder recommends to improve visibility, highest priority first. Without a status filter it lists open and in-progress Actions; each item has its id, target (page, prompt or source), status, priority score, approach and link, and status_counts counts every status. Items come 50 per page by default; pass next_cursor for more. Pass action_id for one Action in full: its diagnosis, each finding with its remediation, the measured outcome and any declaration. Use update_action_status to dismiss or reopen one, and prepare_declare_implemented when its work is done.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

action_id.description: An Action id from a previous list, to read that one Action in full.

status.description: Keep only Actions with this status.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_ai_ads
tools.title: Read ads in AI answers
tools.description: Paid ads shown in ChatGPT Search answers for the latest or a chosen run: ad presence rate ("N of M ChatGPT answers"), advertisers with share and first/last seen, the ad share and best rank of the brand itself, text creatives (paged) and prompts that surface ads with competitor ads beside organic brand mentions. Only ChatGPT Search shows ads; other engines are not_applicable, never zero. Ads are paid placements: report them separately, never as citations, sources or a cause of visibility.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_ai_crawlability
tools.title: Read AI crawler access
tools.description: Read whether the site's robots.txt lets each AI crawler in, for the latest or a chosen crawl: whether robots.txt was fetched (and its status), the sitemaps it lists, and per crawler (such as GPTBot or ClaudeBot) its operator, purpose, the matching rule, root access and how many sampled URLs it may not fetch. This is permission, not observed visits: use read_crawl_logs for crawlers that actually came. unavailable no_site_crawl means no crawl exists; robots_not_observed means the crawl could not read robots.txt.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id that read_site_health returned; omit for the latest crawl.

tools.name: read_ai_referrals
tools.title: Read AI referral traffic
tools.description: Visits that arrived from AI assistants such as ChatGPT, from GA4: sessions, share of all traffic, key events and top landing pages for a range. These are people clicking through; read_crawl_logs has crawler requests. An unavailable state means no referral data has been imported, which is not zero; read_integration_status says why.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

range.description: A preset window ending today; or pass start_date and end_date instead.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

tools.name: read_ai_shelf
tools.title: Read the AI Shelf
tools.description: Read how AI answers recommend products for an ecommerce project: which products and merchants hold the "shelf" when buyers ask for a product category. Call it first with no target to get the catalog: categories with product counts, and up to 200 products with their category ids (products_omitted counts the rest). Then call it again with target_kind and target_id for one category or product: product visibility, share of shelf, average position, first-position win rate, the answer counts they rest on, when it was measured, and the holders (your products, competitors, merchants) with their best rank. unavailable no_product_catalog means the project has no product catalog, which is normal for non-ecommerce brands; use read_visibility_overview for brand mentions instead.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

target_kind.description: Pass together with target_id: whether it names a category or a product.

target_id.description: A category or product id from the catalog this tool returns without a target; pass together with target_kind.

tools.name: read_ai_traffic_insights
tools.title: Read AI traffic insights
tools.description: Read the patterns CiteLadder found by joining AI crawler, referral and citation data for one saved window: pages crawled but never visited from AI, pages getting AI referrals but not crawled recently, crawler errors on valuable pages, and key events concentrated on few pages. Each pattern has a short explanation, the numbers behind it and the pages involved, with coverage. These are co-occurrence, not cause. It reads the newest saved 30-day window by default; custom dates must match a saved window exactly. unavailable means no insight snapshot exists yet, and coverage.notice says why, such as GA4 not being connected. Use read_ai_traffic_pages for the per-page numbers.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

range.description: A preset window ending today; or pass start_date and end_date instead.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

tools.name: read_ai_traffic_pages
tools.title: Read AI traffic by page
tools.description: Rank the project's own pages by AI activity, to find which pages AI crawlers fetch, AI assistants send visitors to and AI answers cite. Each row is one page (URL, path, folder, resource class) with four measures, each carrying its own coverage: AI crawler requests (server logs), AI referral sessions and key events (GA4), citations in AI answers, and Site Health findings, plus its last crawl. The window defaults to the last 30d; rows come 10 per page (up to 100); pass next_cursor for more. observed_crawl_coverage says how complete the logs are, and a measure without a connected source is missing, not zero. Use read_ai_traffic_url for one page's timeline, read_crawl_logs for crawler-level detail, read_ai_referrals for site-wide referral totals, and read_site_pages for crawl data such as titles and scores.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

range.description: A preset window ending today; or pass start_date and end_date instead.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

folder.description: A site path prefix such as /blog/ to read only pages under it.

resource_class.description: A resource_class a previous row returned, such as page, to read only that kind.

verification.description: Keep only crawler requests whose claimed identity was verified, could not be verified, or failed verification.

sort.description: Row order by one measure, highest first, or by URL; omit for the default. Filters (folder, resource_class, verification) apply first.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_ai_traffic_url
tools.title: Read AI traffic for a URL
tools.description: Read the timeline of AI activity on one page of the project site, after read_ai_traffic_pages names it: the page's four measures (crawler requests, referral sessions, citations, Site Health findings) with their coverage and 4xx/5xx errors, then each crawler's first and last visit and request count, each AI source's first referral and sessions, and each citation by date and run. The window defaults to the last 30d. Each timeline is capped, and provenance.bounded is true when a cap was hit. The URL must be on the project's own site. unavailable url_not_joinable means the path cannot be matched (for example a redacted path); unavailable with no reason means no activity was recorded for that page in the window.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

url.description: A page URL on the project site, as read_ai_traffic_pages listed it.

range.description: A preset window ending today; or pass start_date and end_date instead.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

tools.name: read_content_differentiation
tools.title: Read content comparisons
tools.description: Read how the competitor pages AI answers cite differ from your own page on the topics they win. Use it before rewriting a page to compete. It returns up to the 10 newest comparison reports, each with its query, the owned page compared, the features both have (parity), those only competitors have (gaps) and those only you have, each with the share of inspected pages showing it. A report with state insufficient_evidence had fewer than 3 readable competitor pages or no matching owned page. An empty list means no comparison was made yet; this tool never reads new pages. Use read_visibility_sources to find the competing pages first.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: read_crawl_logs
tools.title: Read AI crawler visits
tools.description: Read the AI crawler requests your server logs recorded, to see which crawlers actually visited, what they fetched and what they got back. View summary (the default) gives totals: requests, pages, active crawlers, error share and a daily series by purpose. View crawlers gives one row per crawler with status codes and verification. View coverage says how complete each day of logs is. View requests lists individual requests. The window defaults to the last 30d, except that requests without range or dates reads every retained day. The paged views return 10 rows by default (up to 100) with a top-level next_cursor; changing a filter needs a new first page, while a continuation may change limit. Failed-verification requests are left out unless verification asks for them. connection not_connected or missing coverage means unknown, not zero. Use read_ai_crawlability for robots permission and read_ai_traffic_pages for activity per page.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

view.description: summary is totals; crawlers is one row per AI crawler; coverage is how complete each day of logs is; requests lists individual requests, paged.

range.description: A preset window ending today; or pass start_date and end_date instead.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

verification.description: Keep only crawler requests whose claimed identity was verified, could not be verified, or failed verification.

bot_id.description: A bot_id the crawlers view returned; keep only that crawler.

status.description: An HTTP status code; keep only requests answered with it.

folder.description: A site path prefix such as /blog/ to read only pages under it.

resource_class.description: A resource_class a previous row returned, such as page, to read only that kind.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_demand
tools.title: Read search demand
tools.description: Read the latest search-demand snapshot: the opportunities CiteLadder found in the project's own Search Console data for one window, such as queries in striking distance of page one, pages competing for the same query, click-through below the site's norm and rising or falling queries. It returns the window (pass it to read_query_evidence for the query rows behind it), the signal count by type, each detector's state, coverage (whether search data and query evidence were observed) and the change in signal count against the previous snapshot, which is not a cause. unavailable no_demand_snapshot means no snapshot was built yet, usually because Search Console is not connected or still importing; read_integration_status says which. The signals become Actions: use read_actions for the prioritized work. Keyword volumes from research live in read_search_intelligence.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: read_fact_checks
tools.title: Read fact checks
tools.description: Read whether AI answers state the brand's facts correctly. Factual claims answers made about the brand in the latest or a chosen run are checked against the brand's confirmed facts. The summary view gives accuracy (supported out of supported plus contradicted) with its coverage, by topic and engine, the contradicted claims with the fact they contradict, and sources cited alongside them. The claims view lists every checked claim with its quote, verdict and the facts used, paged (50 by default, pass next_cursor). Use read_perception for tone rather than accuracy. Always state the coverage and quote the fact. accuracy_state not_enabled, no_facts, no_claims, pending or unavailable means there is no value, never zero; inconclusive and not_covered are not errors in the answer. Sources are cited alongside a contradiction, never its cause.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

view.description: summary is accuracy and its coverage; claims lists the checked claims, paged.

topic.description: With view claims: keep only claims about this kind of fact.

verdict.description: With view claims: keep only this verdict; contradicted finds the errors.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_integration_status
tools.title: Read connected data
tools.description: Read which data sources (Search Console, GA4, server logs) are connected to the project and how far their import has got, to explain why a traffic or search read is unavailable. It returns the overall stage (not_connected, connected, importing, core_data_ready, analysis_ready or import_failed), the backfill state and the date data is imported through, whether performance and demand snapshots exist, and each connection with its provider, property and last sync. Read it when another read returns unavailable or not_connected, before reading that again. Connecting a source happens in CiteLadder, not through this tool.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: read_perception
tools.title: Read answer perception
tools.description: Read how AI answers portray the brand and competitors in the latest or a chosen run: net sentiment (-100 to +100) per brand, engine, topic and prompt, each with its coverage; praise and criticism by theme; how often answers recommend or advise against the brand; and the sources cited alongside criticism. The summary view returns all of that; the quotes view lists the verified quotes behind it, paged (50 by default, pass next_cursor). The response is always available: read perception_state, where pending, unavailable or no_mentions means there is no value, never zero. Always state the coverage. Sources are cited alongside criticism, never its cause. Use read_fact_checks for whether answers are factually right, and read_visibility_overview for how often the brand is mentioned at all.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

view.description: summary is sentiment and themes per brand; quotes lists the verified quotes, paged.

entity.description: With view quotes: a brand exactly as the summary names it, to quote only it.

theme.description: With view quotes: keep only quotes about this theme.

polarity.description: With view quotes: keep only praise or only criticism.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_performance
tools.title: Read search performance
tools.description: Read the site's organic search performance from Search Console and GA4: clicks, impressions, CTR, average position, sessions and key events for a window, with a series over time and an optional comparison window. Without dimension it returns totals, the series, data coverage and how many rows each breakdown has; with dimension it returns one page of rows by query, page, country, device or day (10 by default, pass next_cursor for more). The range defaults to last_synced, all imported data; most custom windows have no saved snapshot and return performance_range_not_projected, so prefer the preset ranges. not_connected means no search source is connected, which is not zero; read_integration_status says why. Use read_query_evidence for queries matched to crawled pages, and read_ai_referrals for traffic from AI assistants.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

start_date.description: First day of a custom window, inclusive.

end_date.description: Last day of a custom window, inclusive.

granularity.description: The bucket size of the totals over time.

compare.description: The window to compare against; custom needs the compare dates.

compare_start_date.description: First day of a custom comparison window, inclusive.

compare_end_date.description: Last day of a custom comparison window, inclusive.

dimension.description: Break the totals down by this dimension, paged.

sort.description: With dimension: one of clicks, ctr, dimension_key, impressions, position; prefix - for descending, such as -clicks.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

tools.name: read_prompt_portfolio
tools.title: Read prompts
tools.description: List the prompts the project tracks, so you know what is measured before reading results or changing prompts. Each row has the prompt id, text, topic, intent, buyer stage, cohort (core prompts are scored; comparison prompts name a competitor and are reported separately), status and whether audits measure it now, plus its prompt set and topic_id. topics lists every project topic (id, name, description), including topics with no prompts yet; topics_truncated says the list is partial. Rows come oldest first, 50 per page by default; pass next_cursor for more. To find one prompt by its wording use search; to see what engines answered for a prompt use read_visibility_results with its prompt_id. Prompt ids feed update_prompt_text, prepare_archive_prompts and prepare_launch_audit.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

prompt_set_id.description: A prompt set id from an earlier row of this tool; omit for every set in the project.

cohort.description: Keep only scored or only comparison prompts; combines with the other filters.

active_only.description: true keeps only prompts audits measure now; false (the default) also lists disabled and archived ones.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_query_evidence
tools.title: Read queries by page
tools.description: Read the Search Console queries that bring searchers to each site page, matched to pages CiteLadder crawled, for one saved window. Use it to see which queries a page ranks for, or which page answers a query; for totals and trends use read_performance, and for the search signals found in the same window use read_demand. The window must exactly match a saved one: read_demand returns it. Any other window returns unavailable exact_query_evidence_window_not_projected, which is not zero. Each row is one query, page and day: the query, the page Search Console reported, the crawled page it was matched to (site_url_id), how the match was made (resolution_outcome), and impressions, clicks and CTR. Rows come 50 per page by default; pass next_cursor for more. Country, device and search type are not broken out.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

window_start.description: First day of a saved window, inclusive: read_demand's window.start.

window_end.description: Last day of the same saved window, inclusive: read_demand's window.end.

query.description: One search query, matched exactly ignoring case and spacing, not a search.

site_url_id.description: A page id (site_url_id) from read_site_pages or an earlier row; keep only its queries.

resolution_outcome.description: Keep only queries whose page match was exact, resolved (for example through a redirect or canonical), ambiguous or unresolved. All filters combine.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_search_dataset
tools.title: Read a research dataset
tools.description: Read the rows of one saved keyword or backlink research dataset, after read_search_intelligence has named it. Use it for keyword volumes, rankings, competitor keywords or referring domains; use read_search_intelligence to choose the dataset and read_query_evidence for the project's own Search Console queries. It returns the dataset (kind, target, market, saved row count) and a page of rows (50 by default; pass next_cursor for more, with the same sort), each with a citeladder:// id for fetch. Columns depend on the dataset kind. Referring-domain and page totals are provider aggregates, not individual links: never report them as a link list. Rows are as saved at research time and are never refreshed by this read.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

dataset_id.description: A dataset id from read_search_intelligence; a dataset of another project is refused.

sort.description: The column to order by, which must exist for the dataset kind: one of backlinks, dataforseo_rank, difficulty, domain, etv, id, intent, keyword, owned_rank_group, rank_group, referring_main_domains, search_volume, url, backlinks_spam_score, broken_backlinks, broken_pages, cpc, organic_keywords, rank_absolute, referring_domains, referring_pages. Omit to order by row id. Rows with no value sort last.

direction.description: asc (the default) or desc; desc with a volume or rank column puts the largest first.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_search_intelligence
tools.title: Read keyword and backlink research
tools.description: List the keyword, competitor and backlink research datasets saved for this project, and whether the research provider is connected. Each dataset has its id, kind, target domain, market (location and language), status and whether its totals are aggregates rather than individual links, plus the project's owned targets, tracked competitors and latest research run. It lists datasets only: pass a dataset id to read_search_dataset for its rows. unavailable with no datasets means no research was run yet; this tool never starts research, which happens in CiteLadder. For the project's own Search Console queries use read_query_evidence instead.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: read_site_health
tools.title: Read Site Health
tools.description: Read the Site Health summary of the latest crawl, or a chosen snapshot: the web fundamentals and AI-readiness scores with their measurement state, how many pages were selected and analyzed, and the top 10 issues, each with its rule_id, severity, description, remediation and how many pages it affects. unavailable no_site_snapshot means no crawl was analyzed yet; this tool never starts one. Use read_site_pages with a rule_id to list the affected pages, read_ai_crawlability for robots access, and render_site_health to show the user the interactive view.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

snapshot_id.description: A Site Health snapshot id; omit for the latest crawl.

tools.name: read_site_links
tools.title: Read internal links
tools.description: Read the internal links of crawled pages: per page, inbound and outbound link counts (overall and in main content) and nofollow inbound links, click depth from the home page, a bounded sample of the pages linking to it and linked from it with their anchors, and anchor diagnostics. Use it to find orphaned or buried pages. Pass up to 10 site_url_ids from read_site_pages to read those pages in one call; missing_site_url_ids lists any not found. Otherwise rows come 50 per page; pass next_cursor for more. unavailable no_site_crawl means no crawl exists. Use read_site_pages for page scores and issues.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id that read_site_health returned; omit for the latest crawl.

site_url_ids.description: Page ids (site_url_id) from read_site_pages; omit to page through every page.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_site_pages
tools.title: Read site pages
tools.description: Pages from a crawl, paged: URL, title, page type, status, scores, issue count and the rule ids of each page's issues by finding class. Pass rule_id (from read_site_health top_issues or an issue group) to list exactly the pages affected by that issue; filter by page_kind or status to find pages by type or status. read_site_health gives the totals.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

crawl_id.description: A crawl id that read_site_health returned; omit for the latest crawl.

rule_id.description: A Site Health rule_id; returns only the pages with a current issue of it.

page_kind.description: Keep only pages of this type.

status.description: Keep only pages in this state.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_source_url
tools.title: Read a cited page
tools.description: Read one cited page in depth, after read_visibility_sources or an answer names it: how often it was retrieved and cited, when first and last seen, the engines and models that cite it, the prompts it is cited for (up to 50), the brands it names (up to 12, including whether yours is there), and what CiteLadder read on the page itself. Omit audit_id to cover every run in the market, not just the latest. The URL must match the cited URL exactly; unavailable url_not_cited_in_selection means it was not cited in that selection.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

url.description: A cited URL exactly as read_visibility_sources or an answer listed it.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for every run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

tools.name: read_visibility_overview
tools.title: Read AI visibility
tools.description: Read the headline AI visibility of one run: how often answers mention the brand and cite its site, the visibility score, rankings of the brand against each competitor (mention rate, citation rate, share of voice, average position), a breakdown per engine, and the run's status and answer counts. It defaults to the latest completed run in the default market; pass baseline_id to compare two runs. Each market is measured separately: pass market_id for another market, and never pool markets. unavailable no_completed_run means no run has finished yet. Use read_visibility_trends for change over time, read_visibility_results for the answers themselves, and read_visibility_sources for what was cited.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

baseline_id.description: An earlier run id (audit_id) to compare audit_id against.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

tools.name: read_visibility_results
tools.title: Read AI answers
tools.description: Read the answers engines gave in one run, to see exactly what an engine said for a prompt. Each answer has the prompt text, engine, model, repetition, whether web search was used, the brands mentioned (with first position) and every citation (URL, domain, whether it is your site or a competitor's), plus a citeladder:// id for fetch. audit_id is required: take it from read_visibility_overview. Answers come 50 per page by default; pass next_cursor for more. Only core prompts are included unless cohort is comparison or all. Filters (prompt_id, domain, url, engine) combine. Use read_visibility_overview for rates and read_visibility_sources for citation totals.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id) that read_visibility_overview returned.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

prompt_id.description: A prompt id from read_prompt_portfolio; keep only its answers.

domain.description: A domain such as example.com; keep only rows citing it.

url.description: Keep only answers that cite this exact URL.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_visibility_sources
tools.title: Read cited sources
tools.description: Rank the domains or pages AI answers cited in one run, to find the sources worth earning a place on. Each row has how many answers and prompts cited it, its citation share and rate, ownership (yours, a competitor's or third party) and category; page rows also list up to 3 brands named on the page and whether there is an Action for it. It defaults to the latest run; unavailable no_completed_run means none has finished. Rows come 50 per page by default; pass next_cursor for more. level domain lists publishers; level url, or passing domain, lists pages. Use read_source_url for one page in depth, and read_visibility_results for the answers that cite it.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

audit_id.description: A run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

level.description: domain counts publishers (the default); url counts individual pages.

domain.description: A cited domain such as example.com; with level url, lists its pages.

cursor.description: The next_cursor a previous page returned.

limit.description: How many rows to return; omit for the default page size.

tools.name: read_visibility_trends
tools.title: Read visibility trends
tools.description: Read how visibility changed over an explicit window of at most 366 days, as points per run or per day, week or month. Each point has the visibility score, brand mention and citation rates, share of voice, competitor rankings, the model and whether web search was on, and a comparison_key. Points with different comparison keys were measured differently and are not comparable; gaps are missing runs, not zero. At most the newest 100 points are returned. unavailable no_measured_runs means no run fell in the window. Use read_visibility_overview for one run in depth, or with baseline_id to compare exactly two runs.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

market_id.description: A market id from get_project_business_context; omit for the default market. Markets are never pooled.

from_at.description: Start of the window, with a UTC offset, such as 2026-09-01T00:00:00Z.

to_at.description: End of the window, after from_at and at most 366 days later.

engine.description: Read one engine only; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is the prompts that also name a competitor, reported separately; all is both.

granularity.description: One point per run (the default), or per day, week or month.

transport_model.description: Keep only runs answered by this model, as a previous point named it.

retrieval_enabled.description: true keeps only runs with web search on; false only runs without it.

tools.name: render_site_health
tools.title: Show Site Health
tools.description: Show the user an interactive Site Health view (scores, coverage and top issues) for the latest or a chosen snapshot, in clients that display apps. To reason over the data yourself, use read_site_health.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

snapshot_id.description: A Site Health snapshot id; omit for the latest crawl.

tools.name: render_visibility
tools.title: Show AI visibility
tools.description: Show the user an interactive visibility view, in clients that display apps: overview, trends over a window, or cited sources for one run. To reason over the numbers yourself, use read_visibility_overview, read_visibility_trends or read_visibility_sources.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

view.description: Which view to show; each other field says the views it applies to.

audit_id.description: Overview or sources: a run id (audit_id); omit for the latest run.

snapshot_id.description: Site Health only: a snapshot id; omit for the latest crawl.

engine.description: Show one engine only, such as chatgpt; omit for every engine.

cohort.description: core is the scored prompts (the default); comparison is reported separately.

from_at.description: Trends only, required there: start of the window.

to_at.description: Trends only, required there: end of the window.

transport_model.description: Trends only: keep only runs answered by this model.

retrieval_enabled.description: Trends only: true keeps runs with web search on, false runs without it.

competitor.description: Overview or trends: a competitor exactly as the rankings name it, to highlight.

level.description: Sources only: domain lists publishers (the default); url lists pages.

domain.description: Sources only: a cited domain such as example.com, to list its pages.

cursor.description: Sources only: the next_cursor a previous page returned.

tools.name: search
tools.title: Search
tools.description: Find projects, active Actions and prompts by text when you do not know where a record is. Returns matching records with ids; pass one to fetch for the full record.

query.description: Words to look for, such as a prompt or brand.

project_id.description: Search one project only; omit to search every project.

tools.name: add_competitor
tools.title: Add a competitor
tools.description: Track one more competitor, so visibility reads rank its mentions and citations in AI answers beside your brand. Runs at once; refused if the project already tracks that name or has reached its competitor limit. get_project_business_context lists the competitors tracked now.

name.description: The brand name as buyers write it.

aliases.description: Other names AI answers use for the brand, such as a short form or old name.

domains.description: The brand's own domains, such as example.com, so its cited pages are attributed to it.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: cancel_audit
tools.title: Cancel an audit
tools.description: Stop a queued or running audit, after the user agrees, such as one launched by mistake or on the wrong engines. Runs at once and cannot be undone; answers recorded so far are kept, and no further prompt runs are spent on it. To launch a corrected audit use prepare_launch_audit. Refused if the audit is not in this project or has already finished.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

audit_id.description: A queued or running audit id (audit_id) that read_visibility_overview or confirm_change returned.

tools.name: confirm_change
tools.title: Confirm a prepared change
tools.description: Make a change a prepare tool previewed. Call only after the user explicitly agreed to that preview in this conversation. A token works once, for ten minutes.

confirmation_token.description: The confirmation_token the prepare tool returned, exactly as given.

tools.name: create_topic
tools.title: Create a topic
tools.description: Add a topic, a named group of tracked prompts (for example "Pricing" or "Integrations") that visibility is broken down by. Runs at once and returns the topic id; pass it as topic_id to prepare_add_prompts to file new prompts under it. Topic names are unique in a project, ignoring case.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

name.description: The topic name, unique in the project.

description.description: What prompts under this topic ask about; optional.

tools.name: delete_topic
tools.title: Delete a topic
tools.description: Delete one topic by name, after the user agrees, when the grouping itself is no longer wanted. Its prompts are kept, still tracked, without a topic, and its subtopics become top-level; recorded answers are kept. Runs at once and cannot be undone. To fix only the name use rename_topic; to stop measuring the prompts use prepare_archive_prompts.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: prepare_add_prompts
tools.title: Prepare to add prompts
tools.description: Preview adding 1–50 prompts to a prompt set: which can be added, which are dropped and why, and prompt slots after. Nothing changes until the user agrees and you call confirm_change; confirmed prompts are measured from the next audit.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

prompt_set_id.description: A prompt set id from read_prompt_portfolio; omit when the project has only one prompt set.

text.description: A short question a buyer would ask an AI assistant, answerable by naming a business.

topic_id.description: A topic id from read_prompt_portfolio topics or create_topic; omit for none.

intent.description: What the buyer is trying to do, in a few words; optional.

cohort.description: core prompts are scored (the default); comparison prompts name competitors and are reported separately.

prompts.description: The prompts to add, each a short buyer question.

tools.name: prepare_archive_prompts
tools.title: Prepare to archive prompts
tools.description: Preview archiving tracked prompts so future audits stop measuring them; past results stay. Nothing changes until the user agrees and you call confirm_change.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

tools.name: prepare_declare_implemented
tools.title: Prepare to declare an Action implemented
tools.description: Preview declaring that the work of an open Action is done, so CiteLadder checks later evidence against it. Nothing changes until the user agrees and you call confirm_change.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

action_id.description: An open Action id from read_actions.

declared_implemented_at.description: When the work went live; omit for now. Evidence after it is checked.

tools.name: prepare_launch_audit
tools.title: Prepare to launch an audit
tools.description: Preview launching an audit of a prompt set (or chosen prompts) on the given engines, with the prompt runs it can spend and its maximum provider attempts. Pass market_ids (from the project context; null is the default market) to run one audit per market. Pass max_attempts to cap the attempts. Nothing runs until the user agrees and you call confirm_change.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

prompt_set_id.description: A prompt set id from read_prompt_portfolio; omit when the project has only one prompt set.

prompt_ids.description: Prompt ids from read_prompt_portfolio to audit only those; omit for every active prompt in the set.

engines.description: The AI engines to ask; at least one.

repetitions.description: How many times each prompt is asked per engine; omit for the project default.

market_ids.description: Market ids from get_project_business_context; null is the default market. Omit for the default market only.

max_attempts.description: The most provider attempts the user accepts; omit to use the estimate. The launch is refused if it needs more.

tools.name: prepare_schedule
tools.title: Prepare an audit schedule
tools.description: Preview a recurring audit schedule for a prompt set. Pass market_ids (from the project context; null is the default market) to run one audit per market. Each recorded answer spends one prompt run. Nothing changes until the user agrees and you call confirm_change.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

prompt_set_id.description: A prompt set id from read_prompt_portfolio; omit when the project has only one prompt set.

engines.description: The AI engines to ask; at least one.

timezone.description: An IANA timezone such as Europe/London; omit for the default.

repetitions.description: How many times each prompt is asked per engine; omit for the project default.

interval_minutes.description: Minutes between runs; only for cadence every_n_minutes.

next_run_at.description: When the first run starts; omit to start right away.

market_ids.description: Market ids from get_project_business_context; null is the default market. Omit for the default market only.

tools.name: remove_competitor
tools.title: Stop tracking a competitor
tools.description: Stop tracking one competitor by name, as get_project_business_context lists it, so visibility reads no longer rank it. Recorded answers are kept. Runs at once and cannot be undone; add_competitor tracks it again but its aliases and domains must be given again.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

name.description: The tracked competitor name, ignoring case.

tools.name: rename_topic
tools.title: Rename a topic
tools.description: Rename one topic, after the user agrees. Its prompts and past results stay under it, so prefer this to delete_topic and create_topic when only the name is wrong. Runs at once and returns the new name; refused if another topic in the project already has the name, or if topic_id is not in this project.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

topic_id.description: A topic id from read_prompt_portfolio topics or create_topic.

name.description: The new name, unique in the project.

tools.name: update_action_status
tools.title: Update an Action status
tools.description: Dismiss one Action the user does not want to act on, or reopen a dismissed one. Runs at once. To record that the work was done, use prepare_declare_implemented instead.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

status.description: dismissed hides the Action from the open list; open restores it.

tools.name: update_prompt_text
tools.title: Edit a prompt
tools.description: Replace the wording of one tracked prompt, after the user agrees, such as to fix a typo or make it read like a buyer's question. Runs at once and returns the new wording; earlier measurements keep the old wording, so results before and after the edit may not compare. To stop measuring a prompt use prepare_archive_prompts, and to add new ones prepare_add_prompts. Refused if prompt_id is not in this project.

project_id.description: A project id that list_projects returned.

text.description: The new wording: a short question a buyer would ask an AI assistant.
